name: Arroz Verde (Mexican Green Rice)

cookwares.name: medium saucepan or Dutch oven with lid

ingredients.name: neutral oil, such as canola oil
serrano peppers, stemmed and cut into 1-inch segments
long-grain white rice, rinsed and dried

instructions.primary_message: In a medium Dutch oven or saucepan, heat oil over medium-low heat until shimmering. Add onion, serranos, and garlic. Cook until ingredients soften, about 8 minutes.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer solids to a blender. Add 1/2 cup broth, cilantro, parsley, and epazote, if using. Blend on high until smooth. Season to taste with salt and set aside.
Reheat remaining oil in Dutch oven over medium heat. Add rice and cook, stirring constantly, until the grains are lightly toasted, about 5 minutes. Add blended mixture to rice and stir to coat.

Add remaining 1 cup stock or broth. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat then reduce heat to medium-low to maintain a simmer. Using a wooden spatula, scrape the bottom of the pan multiple times to ensure no rice is stuck. Cover and simmer until liquid is no longer visible on surface of rice, minimal steam is being generated, and rice has a noticeable "cooked" smell, 12 to 18 minutes. Remove from heat and rest, covered, at least 10 minutes or up to 20 minutes. Don't uncover or agitate the rice while resting.
Fluff the rice with a fork. Season with salt to taste and serve with lime wedges.

description: Arroz verde, or Mexican green rice, is a flavorful side that's seasoned with a bright combination of cilantro, parsley, and chiles. It complements seafood, braised vegetables, grilled meats, and more.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 1/2 cup loosely packed fresh epazote leaves (optional, see note); Lime wedges, for serving

Optional substitutions: homemade chicken stock → vegetable stock or store-bought low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth

Notes: Epazote is a Mexican herb with an earthy, minty flavor profile. If you can't find it, you can increase the amount of cilantro or parsley to a full cup.

Make-ahead and storage: The herbal flavor of the rice is best enjoyed fresh, but leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Octavio Peña
